body:
At the fixed Boolean critical exponent, a single normalized vertex spike has arbitrarily large finite limiting density moment and nonvanishing moment tails, while its actual normalized transfer gap tends to 1-rho. A finite-prefix replacement supplies any prescribed floor below one and any strict moment-budget slack, with gap at least (1-rho)/2 in every dimension.

This is a grouped explanatory complement to unit300, not a standalone paper or originality claim. The proof uses Gram isospectrality and an exact rank-one norm; it distinguishes density tails from invariant-measure operator tails and the previous two-spike obstruction. Judges are preregistered in 758e1c5d8d40f3ce4717fc4885c29a5f9dec3559. Separate analytical audit and required repository checks remain gates. No new PDF, numerical grade, formal verification, or local mathematical computation is claimed.
